judged_text: The booking create persists only `evt.destinationCalendar[0]` via the singular `connect`, so the additional collective team calendars exist only in-memory during creation and are never linked to the booking record. Downstream flows that rebuild CalendarEvent from the booking (reschedule, cancel, payment webhooks, bookingReminder) reconstruct at most the organizer's calendar, so the multi-calendar state this PR introduces is not durable and later operations touch only the first destination — the next change to cancellation/reschedule logic has to re-derive the member calendars independently.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and, for COLLECTIVE team events, pushes additional member calendars into `evt.destinationCalendar` (`handleNewBooking.ts`: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`). However, when persisting the booking it still only connects a single `destinationCalendar` via `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`, so only the first calendar is stored on the booking record. Multiple downstream rebuilds of `CalendarEvent` from a booking also only wrap a single `booking.destinationCalendar || user.destinationCalendar` into an array (e.g., `bookingReminder.ts`, payments webhooks, confirm/editLocation handlers), so the multi-calendar list is not durable across reloads. This is a real diff-grounded completeness/architecture concern, even though other parts (e.g., updating/deleting via multiple `_calendar` references) may mitigate some flows.
